notes.1a: This was well answered with a significant number of candidates providing four correct terms.
notes.1b: This was also well answered by most candidates with many preparing a fully correct account. The most common error was the miscalculation of the subscriptions.
notes.1c: Nearly all candidates correctly added their surplus to the given opening balance.
notes.1d: Well answered with most candidates displaying a good knowledge of life membership accounting.
notes.1e: Most candidates gave a recommendation along with appropriate justification. A limited number did disregard the rent saving in appraising the building of the boathouse.
notes.2a: Most candidates explained the meaning of the term ‘revaluation reserve’ reasonably well.
notes.2b: The capital accounts were well prepared with a limited number of fully correct accounts. The most common errors were the omission of the dissolution costs and the incorrect treatment of the settlement of the trade receivables and trade payables.
notes.2c: Well answered with many fully correct sections of the statement. The most common error was the incorrect posting of the share premium value.
notes.2d: Candidates demonstrated a good knowledge of the required shares though some disregarded the cumulative effect of the preference shares.
notes.3a: Most candidates prepared the ledger accounts to a high standard and scored most of the available marks. There were no common errors.
notes.3b: This question was also well answered but a significant number of candidates did not consider the effect on the profit per container as a result of the increased cost.
notes.3c: Relatively few candidates gave an appropriate reason.
notes.4a: Nearly all candidates gave an acceptable explanation with many obtaining both of the available marks.
notes.4b: Nearly all candidates made the calculation correctly.
notes.4c: The statement was prepared to a high standard with some being fully correct. The most common error was the miscalculation of the profit for the year and this was invariably due to not adjusting the debenture interest paid for the period of its issue. Most candidates prepared an appropriate note in respect of the proposed dividend.
notes.4d: Most candidates gave a decision and appropriate justification. Performance was variable with some very good answers but some which were repetitive as well as some which only considered one of the options.
notes.5a: This was generally well answered although some candidates did not deal correctly with the fixed overheads.
notes.5b: Nearly all candidates calculated the total cost of production correctly.
notes.5c: Most candidates calculated the labour variances correctly but relatively few were able to calculate the fixed overhead variances correctly.
notes.5d: The reconciliation was prepared to a high standard with most candidates obtaining at least three of the four available marks.
notes.5e: Most candidates gave a decision but the justification was often less than convincing.
notes.6a: This was well answered with many candidates stating two appropriate benefits.
notes.6b: Again, well answered with some fully correct budgets. Most calculated the receipts correctly. The most common error related to the payments to the suppliers.
notes.6d: This was well answered with a limited number of fully correct statements. The most common error was the omission or miscalculation of the discount allowed.
notes.general_comments:
Overall candidate performance was satisfactory. The quality of the written work as well as the computational
elements was good.
